newsitem.title: UK: UK wants to extend cordless communications.
newsitem.headline: UK wants to extend cordless communications.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Tuesday it wanted to extend telecom licences so that more companies could provide digital cordless telephones.
Asking for comments from companies such as British Telecommunications, the DTI said new digital technologies meant that "no longer does leaving your desk mean losing calls".

Under the proposals, business telephone users would be more mobile -- with companies providing cordless phones at work, home or in hotels -- without the expense of cellular phones. They would also keep the benefits of private branch exchanges (PBXs).

Under proposals for the two new class licences that will extend the Telecommunications Act, the licensing of public access digital cordless communications would be significantly extended, the DTI said.
"I want to see increasing on-site mobility for business users," said Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor in a statement.
"Businesses should be able to enjoy the greater flexibility cordless PBX services bring, with staff no longer being out of touch as they work in and around their offices or sites."
There are over four million cordless phones in the UK and the number is increasing at around 20 percent per year.
Most are residential units using the low cost, older analogue technology.
But there is increasing interest in cordless business communications for both voice and data applications, based on the European DECT and CT2 digital standards.
